【详解】写作步骤

\[第一步：审题立意\]

确定文体：记叙文，使用一般过去时为主，一般现在时为辅

明确要点：①描述一次亲身经历；②经历中的具体做法；③从这次经历学到的东西，可适当拓展

确定人称：第一人称（I）

注意事项：标题与首句已给出，不计入词数；不得透露个人信息；包含全部要点内容

\[第二步：构思布局\]

按“三段式”梳理结构：

开头段：沿用题目给出首句，阐释什么是learning by doing，点明主旨；

主体段：讲述制作喂鸟器的完整亲身经历，交代事件起因、操作过程与现场结果；

结尾段：表达本次实践带来的收获与感悟。

\[第三步：要点展开\]

要点一：解释什么是“做中学”

概念阐释：The best way to learn is to do it ourselves/We learn best by doing things in person...

要点二：讲述自己一次做中学的亲身经历

事件起因：Last Saturday; decided to give it a try; Last weekend; decided to have a try...

制作操作：cleaned and dried a plastic bottle; cut out some holes; hung it from a tree branch; washed a plastic bottle; made some holes; hung it on a tree branch...

事件结果：a little bird landed on the branch and ate from my bottle; a small bird rested on the branch and fed from my bottle...

要点三：写出从这次经历中学到的东西

知识收获：learn more about birds; know more about birds

思想感悟：the importance of caring about lives around us; the value of caring for living things around us...

Do you like music? Have you ever listened to upbeat music—often music that is happy or energetic—to cheer yourself up? Research has shown that music can have an effect on our mind. So, what is the science behind music?

However, if people just listen to the music but don’t actively try to feel happier, they can’t feel better. And listening to slower, more serious music doesn’t help them feel any happier either.

And there’s more. Researchers also found that listening to some classical music helps your brain focus and deal with information better. This is very useful when you’re studying. And many people report that simple and soft music can also help their brain stay focused. Why? The brain has two kinds of attention. One is conscious attention (有意注意) and the other is unconscious attention. While the conscious attention may be focused on work, the unconscious attention may have nothing to do, only looking for fun. Having music on in the background gives the unconscious attention something to focus on, which improves overall concentration (专注力).

The power of music doesn’t stop there. If you have trouble falling asleep from time to time, music can also help. Research shows that the best music for this purpose has about sixty beats per minute—almost the same as a healthy, resting heart. Classical music is often around this speed. Any music that is soft and does not have sudden loud parts may be effective. People who have serious sleep problems may need to listen to this kind of music for several nights before they see results.

A swamp (沼泽) is a wetland, an area in the countryside that is filled with water for most or all of the year. There are swamps all over the world. <u>\_\_\_\_41\_\_\_\_</u> In fact, that isn’t all true. Swamps help reduce pollution in rivers and lakes. They protect our cities from floods. They are home to numerous animals and plants.

A lot of the wildlife is hidden in swamps. There are a huge number of animals there. <u>\_\_\_\_42\_\_\_\_</u> You can even find red-crowned cranes, a national first-class protected animal, walking slowly to catch small fish and insects. Some swamps also serve as protected places for sea animals to grow before they head to the ocean.

<u>\_\_\_\_43\_\_\_\_</u> There are mangrove trees that can live in salt water. The roots of these trees help to protect and build our soil, and they can protect us from extreme weather. There are also strange and beautiful plants that eat insects.

In the past, people removed (抽走) the water from the swamps so they could grow food or build houses on the land. <u>\_\_\_\_44\_\_\_\_</u> Swamps have huge plant and animal diversity. These plants and animals need each other to survive. And we need plant and animal diversity to survive. If we lose the swamps, we will lose a lot. <u>\_\_\_\_45\_\_\_\_</u>

A. We must take care of them!

B. But we know now this isn’t a good idea.

C. Swamps are home to many interesting and important plants.

D. Many people think that swamps are problems, or that they aren’t useful.

E. For example, you can see frogs, wild ducks, bonefish and Chinese water deer.

【导语】本文主要介绍了沼泽的生态价值，纠正了人们过去对沼泽的错误认知，呼吁人们保护沼泽湿地。

【41题详解】下文提到“In fact, that isn’t all true.”，说明空格处内容是一种被后文否定的错误观点，选项D“Many people think that swamps are problems, or that they aren’t useful.”恰好表述了很多人认为沼泽毫无用处、是麻烦的错误认知，和后文的纠正逻辑衔接顺畅。

【42题详解】上文提到“There are a huge number of animals there.”，空格后又列举了丹顶鹤这类保护动物，选项E“For example, you can see frogs, wild ducks, bonefish and Chinese water deer.”是对前文沼泽中存在大量动物的举例说明，前后内容呼应。

【43题详解】空格后文“There are mangrove trees that can live in salt water...There are also strange and beautiful plants that eat insects.”介绍了能在盐水中生存的红树、食虫植物等特殊植物，选项C“Swamps are home to many interesting and important plants.”总起本段内容，引出后文对沼泽特色植物的介绍，逻辑通顺。

【44题详解】上文“In the past, people removed the water from the swamps so they could grow food or build houses on the land.”讲述过去人们抽干沼泽水来种地建房，下文“Swamps have huge plant and animal diversity.”说明沼泽物种丰富，不能被破坏，所以此处要对过去的做法进行否定，选项B“But we know now this isn’t a good idea.”用but转折，表明现在知道这种做法不对，衔接上下文，符合语境。

【45题详解】前文“If we lose the swamps, we will lose a lot.”点明如果失去沼泽人类会损失惨重，选项A“We must take care of them!”发出要保护沼泽的呼吁，作为文章结尾收束全文符合逻辑。
